reflection.text:
Unblinding: alsterpaullone (PubChem CID 5005498, ChEMBL CHEMBL50894, name and BBBC021 structure agree, no curated MoA in lookup e24/e25) – verdict correct: agent Kinase inhibitors p=0.52 (e23) matches truth Kinase inhibitors. Review approved as appropriately cautious.

What got right and why:

Phenotype was a dose-dependent hypertrophic arrest with diluted DNA, not mitotic or cytoskeletal. We spanned the range available (e1: 8 doses 0.01-30uM, 4 wells left) with e4 0.1uM, e2 1uM, e3 10uM, e17 30uM rep1 all. Already at 0.1uM nuc_major_axis z=+4.4, nuc_solidity +3.2 (e4); at 1uM +5.9/+4.5 and nuc_dna_mean -4.4 (e2); at 10uM +9.1/-5.1 (e3); at 30uM frac_large_nucleus +25.5, nuc_major_axis +17.7, nuc_dna_mean -12.4 with cell count dropping 797->923->731->426 (e17). Dose_response confirmed monotonicity over 3-4 wells: nuc_major_axis rho=+1.00 p=0 (e9), nuc_dna_mean rho=-1.00 p=0 (e8), nuc_dna_integrated rho=-1.00 p=0 (e16). That pattern – nuclei getting much larger while mean and integrated DNA content per nucleus decreases – was the key discriminator in e18 hypothesis update (Kinase 0.48 vs DNA damage 0.28 vs DNA replication 0.15).

It correctly argued against DNA damage/replication/Aurora polyploid/G2 arrest expectations which would increase integrated DNA and/or nuc_area with strong monotonic cell loss. Here nuc_area rho=+0.50 p=0.67 (e13), frac_large_nucleus rho=+0.50 p=0.67 (e14), cell_count rho=-0.50 p=0.67 (e11) – no strong dose trend, consistent with arrest/hypertrophy not acute cytotoxicity and no DNA accumulation, despite microscopy noting lower density at 1uM and 30uM (e5,e19) vs similar at 10uM (e6). Literature found in this run describes alsterpaullone as a cyclin-dependent kinase and GSK-3β inhibitor PMID 23577282, PMID 12669310, PMID 30233322, with p38 MAPK-related apoptosis reported PMID 30655881 and antitumor activity in CDK-dependent models PMID 31743514 – compatible with a G1/S block hypertrophy.

Equally important was ruling out microtubule/Eg5/Aurora. Dose_response for tub_mean rho=-0.50 p=0.67 (e10), tub_std rho=0.00 p=1 (e21), act_mean rho=0.00 p=1 (e22), frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.50 p=0.67 (e12) all flat/non-significant, and microscopists gave no cytoskeletal candidates (e5 unknown, e6 none). Selective CDK inhibition is reported to give predominant cell-cycle arrest and senescence-associated enlargement without mitotic spindle changes PMID 38047585, PMID 30905681, PMID 28844647, which matches our flat tubulin/actin/mitotic trends.

What was misleading and why:

compare_to_reference_atlas favored DNA damage throughout: 4/10 vs Kinase 3/10 vs Replication 3/10 at mid-doses (e7) and 5/10 vs 2/10 vs 2/10 after adding 30uM (e20). Eccentricity shift at 10uM z=+3.3 (e3) with rho=+0.50 p=0.67 (e15) and the very large nuclei at 30uM triggered a microscopist candidate of Aurora kinase inhibitors (e19) – understandable given frac_large_nucleus +25.5 (e17) can mimic polyploidy. We missed no measurement, but atlas similarity alone would have driven to DNA damage. The acquisition choice to include the 30uM well and to quantify integrated DNA (e16) and mitotic fraction (e12) prevented that error: no increase in integrated DNA or mitotic fraction despite extreme enlargement, contradicting Aurora/Eg5/microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer and DNA damage polyploidy.

Initial literature searches with narrow phenotype terms returned 0 hits (e26,e27), and phenotype descriptions were vague (e5 7 observations unknown, e6 8 observations none), so we relied on quantitative dose trends rather than atlas or microscopy labels. The 4-well span meant trends were not single-well artifacts as noted in review, though all were rep1 and low-dose cell count variance was not assessed with replicates.

In sum, the decision rested on e8/e9/e16/e17 dose-dependent decondensation/enlargement without DNA gain plus e10/e12/e21/e22 negative cytoskeletal/mitotic signals; atlas DNA-damage plurality and the e19 Aurora suggestion were correctly down-weighted. Next experiment as proposed (PI/EdU + phospho-p38/pERK/Gamma-H2AX vs PD-169316/etoposide) remains appropriate to separate kinase-mediated G1 hypertrophy from G2 damage response without giving clinical advice.
what_was_right: e2-e4,e17 dose-dependent nuclear elongation/enlargement with diluted DNA; rho=+1.00 p=0 (e9) and rho=-1.00 p=0 (e8,e16) supported hypertrophic arrest vs DNA accumulation
e10,e12,e21,e22 flat tubulin/actin/mitotic trends correctly excluded microtubule/Aurora/Eg5
Acquisition spanning 0.1,1,10,30uM (e2-e4,e17) showed onset at low dose and extreme +25.5 SD large-nuclei at high dose, not single-well artifact
what_was_wrong: e7,e20 atlas nearest neighbors favored DNA damage 4-5/10 over Kinase 2-3/10, misleading if taken alone
e19 microscopist Aurora candidate at 30uM based on large nuclei, contradicted by e12 frac_mitotic_like and e16 integrated DNA
e5/e6 vague phenotype descriptions provided no mechanistic anchor until dose trends added
reflection.next_experiment: Flow PI/EdU + phospho-p38/pERK Western and gamma-H2AX IF at 1,10,30uM vs controls as originally proposed

Equally important was ruling out microtubule/Eg5/Aurora. Dose_response for tub_mean rho=-0.50 p=0.67 (e10), tub_std rho=0.00 p=1 (e21), act_mean rho=0.00 p=1 (e22), frac_mitotic_like rho=-0.50 p=0.67 (e12) all flat/non-significant, and microscopists gave no cytoskeletal candidates (e5 unknown, e6 none). Selective CDK inhibition is reported to give predominant cell-cycle arrest and senescence-associated enlargement without mitotic spindle changes PMID 38047585, PMID 30905681, PMID 28844647, which matches our flat tubulin/actin/mitotic trends.

What was misleading and why:

compare_to_reference_atlas favored DNA damage throughout: 4/10 vs Kinase 3/10 vs Replication 3/10 at mid-doses (e7) and 5/10 vs 2/10 vs 2/10 after adding 30uM (e20). Eccentricity shift at 10uM z=+3.3 (e3) with rho=+0.50 p=0.67 (e15) and the very large nuclei at 30uM triggered a microscopist candidate of Aurora kinase inhibitors (e19) – understandable given frac_large_nucleus +25.5 (e17) can mimic polyploidy. We missed no measurement, but atlas similarity alone would have driven to DNA damage. The acquisition choice to include the 30uM well and to quantify integrated DNA (e16) and mitotic fraction (e12) prevented that error: no increase in integrated DNA or mitotic fraction despite extreme enlargement, contradicting Aurora/Eg5/microtubule stabilizer/destabilizer and DNA damage polyploidy.

Initial literature searches with narrow phenotype terms returned 0 hits (e26,e27), and phenotype descriptions were vague (e5 7 observations unknown, e6 8 observations none), so we relied on quantitative dose trends rather than atlas or microscopy labels. The 4-well span meant trends were not single-well artifacts as noted in review, though all were rep1 and low-dose cell count variance was not assessed with replicates.

In sum, the decision rested on e8/e9/e16/e17 dose-dependent decondensation/enlargement without DNA gain plus e10/e12/e21/e22 negative cytoskeletal/mitotic signals; atlas DNA-damage plurality and the e19 Aurora suggestion were correctly down-weighted. Next experiment as proposed (PI/EdU + phospho-p38/pERK/Gamma-H2AX vs PD-169316/etoposide) remains appropriate to separate kinase-mediated G1 hypertrophy from G2 damage response without giving clinical advice.

What was right:
- e2-e4,e17 dose-dependent nuclear elongation/enlargement with diluted DNA; rho=+1.00 p=0 (e9) and rho=-1.00 p=0 (e8,e16) supported hypertrophic arrest vs DNA accumulation
- e10,e12,e21,e22 flat tubulin/actin/mitotic trends correctly excluded microtubule/Aurora/Eg5
- Acquisition spanning 0.1,1,10,30uM (e2-e4,e17) showed onset at low dose and extreme +25.5 SD large-nuclei at high dose, not single-well artifact

What was wrong or missed:
- e7,e20 atlas nearest neighbors favored DNA damage 4-5/10 over Kinase 2-3/10, misleading if taken alone
- e19 microscopist Aurora candidate at 30uM based on large nuclei, contradicted by e12 frac_mitotic_like and e16 integrated DNA
- e5/e6 vague phenotype descriptions provided no mechanistic anchor until dose trends added

Proposed next experiment: Flow PI/EdU + phospho-p38/pERK Western and gamma-H2AX IF at 1,10,30uM vs controls as originally proposed
